messages.subject: extractRawCopyNumbers question
parts:
Hi Henrik,

    I followed your instruction of total copy number analysis for 500k:

    In the last few step, we need to run extractRawCopyNumbers, however, there is no
documents for this function:
?extractRawCopyNumbers()

Non-documented objects      package:aroma.core      R Documentation

Non-documented objects

Description:

     This page contains aliases for all "non-documented" objects that
     'R CMD check' detects in this package.

     Almost all of them are _generic_ functions that have specific
     document for the corresponding method coupled to a specific class.
     Other functions are re-defined by 'setMethodS3()' to _default_
     methods. Neither of these two classes are non-documented in
     reality. The rest are deprecated methods.

Author(s):

     Henrik Bengtsson (<URL: http://www.braju.com/R/>)


(END)

     Since we have two arrays, Nsp and Sty, Should I loop over array=1 and array=2, and  chromosome=1:23 to combine all the results ? or array is always 1, like :
df<-NULL
for ( i in 1:23 ) { rawCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(glad, array=1, chromosome=i); print(rawCNs); rawCNs <- as.data.frame(rawCNs); str(rawCNs); v<-c(i); df2<-data.frame(cbind(rawCNs, chr=rep(v,dim(rawCNs)[1])));  df<-rbind(df,df2) }
write.table(df,args[4], quote = FALSE, sep = '\t',row.names = FALSE,col.names = TRUE);

    Thanks in advacne,
Qicheng

Yes, all help pages that I haven't had time to write point to that
page. The help pages that do exists are mostly for other developers
and not really for end users.

Instead, any end-user documentation for aroma.affymetrix is to be
found online at:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/

Note the 'Pages' section.

My strategy is to document what is stable, i.e. things that are likely
to not change over time. Thus, what you read online is likely to work
the same for awhile.

There are a lot of other bells and whistles in the package that I
still not publish - these are things that are early development and
still haven't matured enough for me to call it stable. This is all a
maintenance strategy of mine; I simply don't have enough time.
However, if people ask for a specific function I occasionally reveal
them. extractRawCopyNumbers() is such a function; it was intended to
be used internally only.

>
> Since we have two arrays, Nsp and Sty, Should I loop over array=1 and
> array=2, and chromosome=1:23 to combine all the results ? or array is
> always 1, like :
> df<-NULL
> for ( i in 1:23 ) { rawCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(glad, array=1,
> chromosome=i); print(rawCNs); rawCNs <- as.data.frame(rawCNs); str(rawCNs);
> v<-c(i); df2<-data.frame(cbind(rawCNs, chr=rep(v,dim(rawCNs)[1])));
> df<-rbind(df,df2) }
> write.table(df,args[4], quote = FALSE, sep = '\t',row.names =
> FALSE,col.names = TRUE);

Yes, extractRawCopyNumbers() operates on a single *chromosome* and a
single *sample/array*, which can consist of CN estimates from multiple
*chip types*, e.g. Mapping250K_Nsp and Mapping250K_Sty.

The method match up data from multiple chip types by the *name* of the
arrays/files. Arrays with the same name can have different *tags* for
the different chip types. They will still be matched up, e.g.

plmData/
MyDataSet,ACC,RMA,FLN/
Mapping250K_Nsp/
OneSample,tagA,2008-01-02,Nsp.CEL
Mapping250K_Sty/
OneSample,Sty,2008-03-23.CEL

It is important that you understand these concepts (names, tags,
fullnames, ...). If not, see the online Page titled 'Names, tags, and
filenames'.

Do mix up sample/array indices with chip types. In your case you have
a set of samples (I cannot tell how many) which you have measurements
from two chip types - Mapping250K_Nsp and Mapping250K_Sty. You do
not have to "merge/interweave/combine" data from the different chip
types yourself - that is done by extractRawCopyNumbers() for you.
However, you'll need to merge CN estimates from multiple chromosomes,
if that is what you want.

See also the thread 'How to extract all CNs?' on Oct 13, 2008:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/8efa8b64c506b5a7

Hope this helps

Henrik

Hi Henrik,

       Thanks for your reply,  I have 3 more questions after reading your email:

1) I read through your instruction of total copy number analysis for 500k, there is no instruction on how to generate  cesN object in "theta <- extractTheta(cesN, units=units, drop=TRUE)" you mentioned in http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/8efa8b64c506b5a7?pli=1

2) I have 7 samples for the ovarian cancer dataset (7 Nsp and and 7 Sty), when  I used  extractRawCopyNumbers to extract Copy Numbers for each sample, why do  I need to loop over 14 arrays instead of 7 arrays to get all the information, since Nsp and Sty are combined into a virtual chip ?

3) "For each location, the raw CN is calculated as the chip effect relative to the chip effect of a normal reference sample.  If no reference sample is available, a robust average across all samples can be used instead.", If I would like to use SNP arrays for all the tumor types as the reference  sample, how can I specify this reference sample when I calculate CN for these 7 ovarian cancer samples.


Thanks,

Qicheng

On Fri, Dec 5, 2008 at 7:50 AM, Qicheng Ma <qiche...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Henrik,
>
> Thanks for your reply, I have 3 more questions after reading your
> email:
>
> 1) I read through your instruction of total copy number analysis for 500k,
> there is no instruction on how to generate cesN object in "theta <-
> extractTheta(cesN, units=units, drop=TRUE)" you mentioned in
> http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/browse_thread/thread/8efa8b64c506b5a7?pli=1

That is the ChipEffectSet you typically get out from doing
fragment-length normalization, cf.

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis

In that vignette 'cesN' corresponds to cesNList[[chipType]]. Since
you have two chip types you will get two different 'cesN' objects. If
you use extractTheta() on these, you'll have to merge the theta
yourself. So, you have to be careful. It is much easier if you just
work of a single chip type.

>
> 2) I have 7 samples for the ovarian cancer dataset (7 Nsp and and 7 Sty),
> when I used extractRawCopyNumbers to extract Copy Numbers for each sample,
> why do I need to loop over 14 arrays instead of 7 arrays to get all the
> information, since Nsp and Sty are combined into a virtual chip ?

There are 14 hybridizations but only 7 samples. You only need to
"loop over" the 7 samples (argument still called 'arrays' for various
reasons). You *must* make sure that you get the names correct for Nsp
and Sty so that the package can pair them up for you. If you don't,
it will think that there are 14 samples where 7 where hyb'ed on Nsp
and the other 7 on Sty.

When you do

cbs <- CbsModel(cesNList);
print(cbs);

make sure that it reports 7 arrays and you can check the names by

print(getNames(cbs));

>
> 3) "For each location, the raw CN is calculated as the chip effect relative
> to the chip effect of a normal reference sample. If no reference sample is
> available, a robust average across all samples can be used instead.", If I
> would like to use SNP arrays for all the tumor types as the reference
> sample, how can I specify this reference sample when I calculate CN for
> these 7 ovarian cancer samples.

I'm not use what you mean by "to use SNP arrays" - do you have another
set of samples you haven't mentioned above?

If you don't specify any reference, the robust average of all samples
will be used. So, if you have 7 cancer samples from the beginning and
don't specify the reference, the pool of them will be used as the
reference.

Hope this helps

Henrik
